meta.description: Industry folders and occupation objects for the Occupation Knowledge Hub. One folder per industry, one object per occupation. Every object can carry one instance of the tool.
meta.sourceNote: Curated starter catalogue of 428 occupations that can be practised in Canada. Grouped by industry for students; the education route follows the NOC 2021 TEER logic, and every occupation is mapped to one graduation department for catalogue filtering (45 departments in 15 faculties). The detailed study path stays in the occupation dossier. Occupation titles use common Canadian usage. This is not the full 516-unit-group NOC list - use the official NOC or Job Bank to add an occupation that is missing. Video links come from two verified Canadian sources: WorkBC's Career Trek and ALIS, the Alberta career information service. Each object also carries a career stage (entry, experienced or leadership) and a short usual path for senior roles; the catalogue uses them for filtering, while the CMS importer ignores them. Version 1.7.0 adds 44 occupation targets mapped from JIBC programs and current AI, drone, space, bio and energy technology roles.
meta.importNote: Same pattern as the tool-ideas folder import: the importer consumes folders[] first, then objects[]. Folders are created in the order given. Objects are matched by slug, so re-running the import skips an occupation that already exists. For a nested 5-group folder tree, import folder-hierarchy-import.json first; its 20 leaf slugs match objects[].industry. The flat folders[] here remains the single-file fallback. The importer must ignore media, resources, videoSources, departments, careerStage and careerPath.

importContract.folders: Create one folder per folders[] entry under the application that owns targetObjectType, keeping name, slug, code and order.
importContract.objects: Create one object per objects[] entry: name = name, slug = slug, parent folder = the folder whose slug equals industry, cmsObjectType = targetObjectType.
importContract.seed: Optional: seed the html-tool field targetFieldId with { version: 1, occupation: { title: name, slug: slug, category: <folder name>, oneLiner: blurb, status: 'draft' } }. The tool normalizes every missing part.
importContract.idempotency: Match objects by slug inside the folder. Skip an object that already exists; never overwrite an edited dossier.

educationRoutes.label: Master's or doctorate
educationRoutes.note: University graduate degree, often required for regulated professions

media.note: Reference metadata only. The importer must ignore objects[].media completely: it must not create fields, objects or folders from it, and it must not fail an import when media is missing or changed. Video links were read from the official Career Trek and ALIS channels; they are not occupation records. See videoSources for the source evaluation register.

videoSources.label: WorkBC's Career Trek
videoSources.note: Primary source: official occupation explainer videos, read from the channel and its industry playlists. It supplied 176 links across 174 occupations before the ALIS pass.

videoSources.label: ALIS Occupational Videos
videoSources.publisher: Alberta Learning Information Service, Government of Alberta
videoSources.note: Official day-in-the-life occupation videos. The playlist holds 255 entries; the first 100 were readable in one pass. ALIS now supplies 63 links: 21 added to existing occupations and 42 attached to the new occupation records. The matches include roofer, concrete finisher and insulator videos found through the playlist, a related-video list and targeted searches. Each link was read from an official ALIS page, and watch pages were verified against alis.alberta.ca.

videoSources.label: Job Talks
videoSources.publisher: Job Talks, Canadian employment marketing and research agency
videoSources.note: Credible Canadian source with professionally filmed worker interviews, but the catalogue is trades-heavy and most matching trades already carry a Career Trek or ALIS video. Exact video IDs for the remaining gaps could not be verified from the channel search page, so no link was added.

videoSources.label: WorkBC
videoSources.note: Official channel, but its videos cover general employment services rather than individual occupations.

videoSources.label: ECO Canada
videoSources.note: Sector council channel, but the uploads are webinars, certification sessions and testimonials, not occupation explainers.

videoSources.label: go2HR
videoSources.publisher: go2HR, BC tourism and hospitality sector council
videoSources.note: Sector council channel, but the uploads are training and webinar content, not occupation profiles.

videoSources.label: Job Bank Canada
videoSources.note: No YouTube channel at the checked handle. Job Bank is still used as a text resource link.

videoSources.label: Health Careers BC
videoSources.note: No YouTube channel at the checked handle, so no videos could be verified.

careerStages.label: Entry level
careerStages.description: First role after the listed education or training; no prior related work experience required.

careerStages.label: Experienced
careerStages.description: Usually requires prior related work experience; may be a first-line supervisor or a specialized role.

careerStages.label: Leadership
careerStages.description: Management, executive or appointment role reached after substantial experience; not a direct entry occupation.

resources.note: Canada-wide explainer links. The catalogue page shows a Job Bank search built from each occupation name plus the NOC and WorkBC links. Reference only: the importer must ignore this key.
